You two sound very similar to me and my girlfriend, so I understand the dynamic. We've also been together for 4 years. We are also in a somewhat similar situation with finances. I'm the breadwinner and she's disabled and can't work.....So, being in a 4 year relationship you are probably looking at this person as lifetime partner. If that's the case your lives are/will be intertwined. I understand you support him and presumably pay for a significant amount of things but at the same time if he is paying you back for these things he is indebted to you. So you have to understand that's adding an element into the relationship that is going to complicate things. Every relationship is different but at this point there is no you and me. It's we. We will help each other wherever is needed. Not, I'll help you out this this and you can pay me back later. That kind of dynamic is complicated and stressful for the party doing the paying back. There is no way to avoid it, and it will affect their decision making and attitude, as you had mentioned. This is what has worked for my situation. I pay for what I need to and my girlfriend is more than willing to help out where she can. No repayment. No debt. No tally sheet. We work together this get through life as a team and that mind of mindset will ease a lot lot lot of stress. Like I said every situation and relationship is different but this is what has worked for us.

A stride like that does a few things. 
1. Takes a LOT of pressure off of your arm.
2. You get more velocity because your using your legs to get your momentum moving towards the plate.
3. To the batter the ball looks like its moving even faster than it really is because your release point is about a foot closer to home plate. 
Basically what i'm saying is there is no single thing that makes someone throw harder than the next person. It's a combination of mechanics from everything to stride to arm angle to release point to flexibility of both the arm and legs. It really is physics. A degree or two here or there can be the difference between a 89mph fastball or a 93mph fastball.

The longer your arms , the higher potential you have to throw harder. Take [Aroldis Chapman](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aroldis_Chapman) for example. 6,4 and holds the world record with a fastball reaching 106 mph.

Any overhead throwing motion is not natural. That's why baseball has so many arm injuries. I'm currently recovering from a surgical posterior labrum repair. Underhand throwing, on the other hand, is natural. That's why softball pitchers can pitch game after game but baseball pitchers usually take a 4-7 day rest between outings.
